To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ketolide antibiotics, like macrolide drugs, are capable of inducing the expression of inducible erythromycin resistance genes.
(i) ketolides are inducers of erm(C) and (ii) the erm(C) induction by ketolides is dependent on the leader peptide.
ketolides, which are generally regarded as noninducers, induce erm(C) expression in E. coli, albeit with kinetics slower than that observed with macrolide antibiotics and to a lower extent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of resistance to antibiotics.
the effects of subinhibitory ketolide concentrations on the expression of erm genes.
the induction of erm(C)-mediated resistance in E. coli by noninducing macrolides and ketolides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ketolides, although generally perceived to be poor inducers of erm genes, are capable of inducing erm gene expression, but the level and rate of induction are lower than those of inducing macrolide drugs.
all macrolides, including ketolides, can induce the expression of erm genes.
the ketolides are inducers of inducible erythromycin resistance, but their potency is lower than that of the 14-member-ring antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ketolides are inducers of inducible macrolide resistance genes.
the ketolides are inducers, but they are weaker inducers than the 14-member-ring drugs.
ketolides, like macrolides, are inducers of erm(C).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induction of erm(C)-like genes should be taken into consideration when ketolides are used for treatment of bacterial infections.
the presence of ketolides in the environment may contribute to the spread and maintenance of erm genes.

the induction of inducible resistance genes is not a binary phenomenon but is rather a continuous process, and that the induction of resistance by a particular drug is not an all-or-nothing phenomenon.
